proved_step: LEMMA (structure of the MMW19 Lemma 3.1 gate tree, sub-part (i) of G0001). Setting: d >= 2, the construction of Lemma 3.1 with leaves D0_x (x in {0,1}^n, one per truth-table bit) and layers i = 1..log_d(2^n); gate G_ij = Circuit-Min-Merge(D_{i-1, jd}, ..., D_{i-1,(j+1)d-1}, intervals). (a) Every description D_{i-1,k} (i-1 >= 0) is an input of exactly one gate G_ij, namely j = floor(k/d): the blocks {jd..(j+1)d-1} are disjoint and cover the layer. (b) The output flag bit of G_ij (its first output bit) is read by the parent gate and, in the MCSP version, by the top AND gate: fan-out 2; in the search version the flag of the root is read by the output AND only. (c) Total gates = sum over layers of ceil(prev/d), which the lab check (own counting code) shows is <= 2^n/(d-1) with depth = ceil(log_d 2^n). Proof of (a),(b): read the construction text (block partition of each layer; the output gate is the AND of the first output bit of each G_ij) - a direct reading, not a new theorem. Consequence: the gate-level graph has NO reuse of intermediate descriptions, so the unfolding of the gate tree equals the tree itself; the abstract layered DAG model in cm-32ceef23cf324b42 (which assumed reuse) does not describe this construction.

proved_step: LEMMA (repaired gate count for the MMW19 Lemma 3.1 tree; replaces S0003(c), see G0004). Let n >= 1, d >= 2, N_0 = 2^n, N_i = ceil(N_{i-1}/d) for i >= 1, D = least index with N_D = 1, G = sum_{i=1..D} N_i. Then (a) N_i = ceil(2^n / d^i) and D = ceil(log_d 2^n); (b) (d-1)*G <= 2^n - 1 + d*D. PROOF. (a) iterated ceiling division ceil(ceil(x/a)/b) = ceil(x/(ab)) for positive integers. (b) For integer x >= 0, ceil(x/d) <= x/d + 1, so N_i <= N_{i-1}/d + 1. Summing over i = 1..D: G <= (1/d) sum_{i=0}^{D-1} N_i + D. Telescoping: sum_{i=0}^{D-1} N_i = N_0 + (G - N_D) = 2^n + G - 1. Hence dG <= 2^n + G - 1 + dD, i.e. (d-1)G <= 2^n - 1 + dD. QED. Evidence: finite check cm-b51193b18e4e4a8b (n <= 20, 2 <= d <= 40: 0 violations, min slack 2), supporting only. Author session R1552 (claude-haiku-5-5) is the same model family as this reviewer, so this reviewer cannot give the cross-family review. Scope: gate count only; says nothing about formula size of the replaced tree, which is G0001(ii).

CORRECTION (R1552, turn 18) to G0005: 'max reads per input bit' is not the right obstacle by itself. Layers compose multiplicatively: if each gate's replacement reads each of its input bits at most r times, leaf counts multiply by about r per layer, so after D = log_d(2^n) layers the leaf count is about r^D = N^(log_d r) with N = 2^n. So c = log_d r < 1 iff r < d, with d = l(n)/(100 s(n) log s(n)). HEURISTIC, NOT PROVED: the accounting ignores the l-fold input fan-in of each gate and the description-bit encoding; both must be included before the threshold r < d is trusted. S0005 (gate count) is unaffected and does not bound this. No P vs NP progress is claimed. S0003(c) is REFUTED by cm-99c4660cd54e4e6f; parts (a),(b) remain unreviewed (same model family as author, so no cross-family review here).

evidence: Part (c) was already refuted by cm-99c4660cd54e4e6f. Parts (a) and (b) describe the basic topology of the MMW19 Lemma 3.1 construction: it is a d-ary tree where each input description $D_{i-1,k}$ is fed into exactly one merge gate $G_{ij}$ (disjoint partitioning of $2^n$ leaves), and the flag bit is passed upward. This structural layout is a direct consequence of the 'Circuit-Min-Merge' definition in MMW19 Sec 4. No internal reuse of descriptions occurs between gates at the same level. Verified against the primary source text (Lemma 3.1).

The proof of S0005(a) relies on the standard identity ceil(ceil(x/a)/b) = ceil(x/(ab)). The proof of S0005(b) uses the bound ceil(x/d) <= x/d + 1. Summing N_i <= N_{i-1}/d + 1 from i=1 to D gives G <= (1/d) sum_{i=0}^{D-1} N_i + D. Since sum_{i=0}^{D-1} N_i = N_0 + (G - N_D) = 2^n + G - 1, we get G <= (2^n + G - 1)/d + D, which rearranges to (d-1)G <= 2^n - 1 + dD. The logic is mathematically sound and the finite check cm-b51193b18e4e4a8b confirms it for n <= 20.

proved_step:
statement: For integers n >= 1, d >= 2, let N_0 = 2^n, N_i = ceil(N_{i-1}/d) for i = 1..D, where D is the first index with N_D = 1, and G = sum_{i=1..D} N_i. Then (d-1)*G <= 2^n - 1 + (d-1)*D, hence also (d-1)*G <= 2^n - 1 + d*D.
derivation: For integer x >= 1: ceil(x/d) <= (x-1)/d + 1, so d*N_i <= N_{i-1} - 1 + d. Sum over i=1..D: d*G <= sum_{i=0}^{D-1} N_i - D + d*D. Since sum_{i=0}^{D-1} N_i = N_0 + G - N_D and N_D = 1: d*G <= N_0 + G - 1 - D + d*D, i.e. (d-1)*G <= N_0 - 1 + (d-1)*D. QED. Finite check: cm-e082d5a32b604f2e, n=1..20, d=2..11, 0 violations of the sharp and weak forms; the old bound G <= 2^n/(d-1) fails in 160 cases.
